## Two points from the literature {#two-sentences-worth-keeping}

::: {.claimcard}
"the common single-path analyses in social and behavioural research should not be simply assumed to be robust to alternative analyses" [@AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness]
:::

::: {.claimcard}
A blueprint: precise question → causal reasoning (DAG) → multiverse → sensitivity analysis [@AuspurgBruderl2021HasCredibilitySocial]
:::

::: {.small}
- Same-conclusion robustness and same-*number* robustness are different bars
- Justifiability is the criterion – choose with reasons, show the spread
:::

::: notes
The first point comes from the Multi100 paper: single-path analyses should not simply be assumed robust. A single path can be a good path, and still the reader is owed the space around it, so a report needs the chosen path and the alternatives together. From Auspurg and Brüderl comes the constructive recipe that we followed today: a precise question, explicit assumptions drawn as a graph, a multiverse, and a sensitivity analysis. And keep the two robustness standards apart in your own writing: the same conclusion, which was reached by seventy-four per cent of the reanalyses in Multi100, and the same number, which only thirty-four per cent came close to. When you claim robustness, say which one you mean.
:::
